description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—as defined in the legend, under a “Zero-Shot” setting. In the “easy” chart, N+K+ (teal) dominates at 55.4%, followed by N−K+ (tan) at 38.3%, N−K− (light brown) at 4.6%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows N+K+ (teal) at 58.8%, N−K+ (tan) at 35.4%, N−K− (light brown) at 4.0%, and N+K− (reddish-brown) at 1.8%. In the “hard” chart, N−K− (light brown) and N−K+ (tan) are nearly equal at 37.9% and 37.3% respectively, while N+K+ (teal) accounts for 18.1% and N+K− (reddish-brown) for 6.7%. All charts include percentage labels within each slice and use consistent color coding per category across difficulty levels, with no slices exploded or emphasized. The visual suggests a shift in category dominance from N+K+ in easier tasks to N−K+ and N−K− in harder ones, reflecting performance trends in geometric knowledge reasoning with large language models as described in the referenced paper.
